ket_qua.ghi_chu: The island government's history confirms Pieter Groen's arrival after the Emily shipwreck in 1836, while historical accounts of the Italia wreck identify the two Italian survivors who remained on the island; both events occurred after the founding settlement.

ket_qua.ghi_chu: The UN confirms Napoleon's exile on St Helena from 1815 to 1821, while official island information identifies St Helena as the nearest inhabited community, approximately 2,437 km north of Tristan.

ket_qua.statement: Britain took Tristan da Cunha in 1816 because it feared France could use the island as a base for an attempt to rescue Napoleon from St Helena, and to stop American ships using it as a base as they had during the War of 1812.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The official island history confirms both strategic concerns: preventing a possible French rescue attempt involving Napoleon on St Helena and preventing American ships from using Tristan as a base during the Anglo-American War of 1812–1814.

ket_qua.ghi_chu: The official island history confirms that a British garrison aboard HMS Falmouth took possession of Tristan da Cunha on 14 August 1816 on behalf of King George III.

ket_qua.ghi_chu: Historical records confirm that Corporal William Glass, a Scot serving in the Royal Artillery, received permission to remain with his wife Maria and two children when the garrison was withdrawn; two other men also remained.

ket_qua.ghi_chu: The official island history confirms all four settlers and their stated arrival years: Thomas Swain in 1826, Pieter Groen in 1836 after the Emily shipwreck, Thomas Rogers in 1836 and Captain Andrew Hagan in 1849.

ket_qua.statement: All land on Tristan da Cunha is held in common, and outsiders are not permitted to buy land on the island.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The Tristan Government explicitly states that all land is communally owned and outsiders are not allowed to buy land or settle on the island.

ket_qua.statement: Potatoes on Tristan da Cunha are grown in the same walled plots at the Potato Patches year after year, without crop rotation.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The Tristan Government explicitly confirms that potatoes are grown year after year on the same plots at the Patches without crop rotation.

ket_qua.statement: On Tristan da Cunha, surplus potatoes are fed to cattle.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The Tristan Government explicitly states that surplus potatoes are used for cattle feed.

ket_qua.statement: The Tristan rock lobster fishery is the foundation of Tristan da Cunha's economy, and the island's coat of arms (granted in 2002) is supported by two Tristan rock lobsters.

ket_qua.ghi_chu: The MSC's 17 December 2020 article states that the lobster fishery contributes 80% of the territory's revenue; the Tristan Government identifies lobster-industry royalties as an important source of foreign earnings alongside stamp and coin sales, without specifying a percentage.

ket_qua.ghi_chu: The Tristan da Cunha Government confirms that the Island Council sets a quota of one adult breeding cow per household; livestock numbers, including sheep, are restricted to conserve pasture and prevent overgrazing.

ket_qua.statement: The 1961 eruption on Tristan da Cunha formed a new volcanic cone and lava flow immediately east of the Settlement, only a few hundred feet from the village.

ket_qua.statement: Earth tremors were felt on Tristan da Cunha from August 1961, in the weeks before the October 1961 eruption.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The official island history records earthquakes and landslides during August and September 1961, preceding the October eruption.

ket_qua.statement: On 8 October 1961 an earthquake and landslide hit the east of the Settlement; the next morning a fissure opened between the Settlement and the canning factory and the ground rose, and the islanders and expatriates were evacuated to huts at the Potato Patches for that night.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The island's official website confirms the 8 October earthquake and landslide, the fissure and ground uplift the following morning, and the overnight evacuation of 264 islanders and 31 expatriates to the Potato Patches.

ket_qua.statement: On 9 October 1961 a fissure opened between the Settlement and the fish cannery and the ground bulged; on 10 October it developed into a new volcanic cone and the island was evacuated.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The official chronology confirms that the fissure opened on 9 October, the rising ground developed into a volcanic cone by 10 October, and the island was evacuated.

ket_qua.statement: On 10 October 1961 the fishing vessels Tristania and Frances Repetto took the evacuated population of Tristan da Cunha to Nightingale Island, where they spent the night.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The official historical account confirms that Tristania and Frances Repetto transported the evacuated population to Nightingale Island on 10 October for overnight shelter.

ket_qua.ghi_chu: The Royal Society expedition confirmed that the lava destroyed the local canning factory while most of the settlement escaped undamaged.

ket_qua.statement: From January 1962 the evacuated Tristan islanders were housed at a former Royal Air Force camp at Calshot, near Southampton, Hampshire, after first staying at Pendell Camp in Surrey.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The islanders were initially accommodated at Pendell Camp in Surrey before moving to former RAF Calshot on 23 January 1962.

ket_qua.statement: In England the Tristan islanders had little immunity to influenza, and they also endured the harsh winter of 1962–63.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: A December 1961 parliamentary answer confirms their unusual susceptibility to colds and influenza because of previous isolation from viruses, while the Tristan historical record confirms influenza epidemics during the severe winter of 1962–63.

ket_qua.statement: On 24 July 1962 the UK Colonial Secretary told Parliament that the Tristan islanders should remain in Britain, citing the risk of further eruptions and the difficulty of maintaining services and landing on the island.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: On 24 July 1962 Secretary of State for the Colonies Duncan Sandys stated that the Government considered remaining in Britain the best course, citing another eruption, difficulties maintaining services and living standards, and the increased difficulty of landing or leaving the island.

ket_qua.statement: A survey party of twelve Tristan islanders left England in August 1962 and reached Tristan da Cunha in early September 1962 to inspect the island.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The historical account confirms that a resettlement survey party including 12 islanders left on 9 August 1962 and returned to Tristan on 8 September 1962 to assess conditions and prepare the settlement for possible resettlement.

ket_qua.statement: In December 1962 the British Colonial Office arranged a ballot of the Tristan islanders in England, who voted 148 to 5 in favour of returning to Tristan da Cunha.
ket_qua.ghi_chu: The official historical account confirms the December 1962 Colonial Office ballot and the 148–5 vote in favour of returning.

ket_qua.statement: An advance party of Tristan islanders arrived back on Tristan da Cunha in April 1963.
